common_name: Desdemona Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Desdemona's compact, healthy habit and pale color make it a versatile choice for a white-and-pastel border scheme.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2015, Desdemona produces ruffled, blush-white buds that open to nearly pure white, cupped rosette flowers with a strong myrrh fragrance carrying hints of almond, held on a compact, well-branched, disease-resistant shrub. Its pale coloring and refined flower form make it a versatile pairing with almost any companion color, and it repeat-blooms freely from late spring through frost with routine feeding and deadheading.

common_name: Vanessa Bell Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Vanessa Bell blooms heavily and benefits from regular deadheading to keep the semi-double flowers coming through the season.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2016 and named for the Bloomsbury Group painter, Vanessa Bell carries semi-double, soft butter-yellow flowers that fade toward cream as they age, with a fresh, tea-and-lemon fragrance, on a healthy, free-flowering, medium-sized shrub. Its semi-double form exposes more stamens than fully double English roses, giving a slightly looser, more relaxed look that also makes it useful to pollinators, and it repeat-blooms reliably from late spring through frost with routine feeding and deadheading.

common_name: Roald Dahl Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Roald Dahl is bred for strong disease resistance and reliably repeats through the season with routine feeding and deadheading.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2016 and named for the celebrated children's author, Roald Dahl bears warm peachy-pink, cupped rosette flowers with a light, fresh tea fragrance, on a healthy, compact, disease-resistant shrub bred to hold clean foliage through humid summers with minimal spraying. It flowers freely and repeats reliably from late spring through frost, making it a dependable, easy-care choice for gardeners wanting classic English-rose form without a demanding maintenance routine.

common_name: A Shropshire Lad Rose (David Austin English Climbing Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation and support for training, since A Shropshire Lad is vigorous enough to be grown as a short climber against a wall, fence, or pillar.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, providing a trellis, pillar, or fence if training the vigorous canes upward. Introduced by David Austin in 1996 and named for the A. E. Housman poetry collection, A Shropshire Lad carries large, softly cupped, warm peachy-pink blooms with a light, fruity fragrance, on long, arching canes that can reach 8-10 feet or more when trained as a climber, or be kept pruned as a large freestanding shrub. Its vigor and long, flexible canes make it a favorite for growing over an arch or pergola, and it repeat-blooms well from late spring through frost with routine feeding and deadheading.

common_name: Emily Brontë Rose (David Austin English Shrub Rose)

planting.note: Set out own-root or container plants in spring or fall in full sun with good air circulation; Emily Brontë blooms in generous flushes and benefits from regular deadheading to sustain repeat flowering through the season.

directions: Plant in full sun in fertile, well-drained soil enriched with compost, and prune canes back by about a third in late winter to encourage strong new flowering wood. Introduced by David Austin in 2018 and named for the author of Wuthering Heights, Emily Brontë bears warm pink, rosette-shaped flowers with a fresh tea fragrance, on a healthy, well-branched, medium-sized shrub bred for improved disease resistance over older English rose cultivars. It flowers in generous flushes from late spring through frost, and its manageable size and clean foliage make it a reliable choice for a mixed border where a compact, classic-form English rose is wanted.
